mainTopic: How men and women (and a כהן and a כהנת) differ in the משנה's list, the end of פרק היה נוטל, and the opening of פרק ארוסה about women who do not drink.
overview: The גמרא first finishes the earlier discussion: even the רבנן agree with רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון about the מנחה of a סוטה married to a כהן. Then it goes line by line through the משנה's list of differences between a כהן and a כהנת: whose מנחה is burned, who can become a חלל, who may become impure from the dead, and who eats קדשי קדשים. Each rule is traced to a פסוק that speaks about males. Next comes the list of differences between a man and a woman. These cover a מצורע's hair and clothing, making a son a נזיר, using a father's נזירות offerings, betrothing or selling a daughter, being stoned naked, being hanged, and being sold for theft. Most come from a male word in a פסוק like 'איש' or 'אותו'. The two נזיר laws are a הלכה according to רבי יוחנן. For stoning, the גמרא shows that 'אותו' cannot mean women are never stoned; it means a man is stoned without clothes. The פרק היה נוטל then ends with a הדרן. A new פרק begins with a משנה: an ארוסה and a שומרת יבם do not drink the bitter water and do not collect a כתובה. The משנה then starts listing women in forbidden marriages, and that list continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Even the רבנן agree about the סוטה's מנחה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא limits the argument between the רבנן and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון to a sinner's מנחה brought by a כהן. In the case of a סוטה's מנחה, everyone agrees.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן only argue with רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון about a כהן's sinner's meal-offering, because that kind of offering is fit to be put on the altar. In our case, even the רבנן agree.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the earlier discussion by showing that the dispute does not reach our case. About the סוטה's מנחה, even the רבנן agree with רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן disagree only about a מנחת חוטא of a כהן, because that offering is 'בת הקרבה', the kind of offering that can go on the altar. The סוטה's מנחה does not have that feature. So even the רבנן agree that after the קמיצה (the handful taken from the offering) its remainder is scattered on the place of the ashes.

keyTerms.meaning: They disagree
The meal-offering brought by a sinner
Fit to be offered on the altar
They agree

steps.whatToRemember: The argument between the רבנן and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון is only about a כהן's מנחת חוטא. About the סוטה's מנחה, everyone agrees.

phrases.english: And even the Rabbis do not disagree with him,
with Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Shimon,
except regarding the sinner's meal-offering of priests,
since it is fit to be offered.
But in this case, even the Rabbis agree.
phrases.notes: 'This case' is the מנחה of a סוטה who is married to a כהן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Wraps up the discussion from before this section about a סוטה's מנחה when she is married to a כהן.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The dispute is limited to a כהן's מנחת חוטא. In the case of the סוטה's מנחה, everyone agrees.

steps.title: Why is a priest's wife's meal-offering burned?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about a בת ישראל married to a כהן and asks for the reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'A בת ישראל who is married to a כהן...' What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line in the משנה and asks where its rule comes from. This step sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה taught two things. A בת ישראל married to a כהן has her מנחה burned, so her husband's status does matter there. A כהנת married to a ישראל has her מנחה eaten. The גמרא wants a source, and the answer explains why a כהנת's מנחה is not treated like a כהן's own מנחה, which is completely burned.

keyTerms.meaning: A Jewish woman who is not from a כהן's family
Etc.; the rest of the quote is assumed
What is the reason?

phrases.english: An Israelite woman who is married, etc.
phrases.notes: The full משנה: if she is married to a כהן her מנחה is burned; a כהנת married to a ישראל has hers eaten.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the source that a woman's מנחה, even a כהנת's, is not treated as a כהן's מנחה that is completely burned?

steps.title: The verse says 'priest' and not 'priest's daughter'
steps.stepSummary: The rule comes from the פסוק 'וכל מנחת כהן כליל תהיה'. It speaks about a כהן, a male, and not a כהנת.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'Every meal-offering of a כהן shall be completely burned; it shall not be eaten.' A כהן, but not a כהנת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק. The burning rule is said about a כהן, so it does not apply to a woman, even one from a כהן's family.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'כהן' is read in a narrow way: only a male כהן's מנחה is כליל, completely burned. A woman's מנחה is never treated as a כהן's own מנחה. So a כהנת married to a ישראל has the handful taken and the rest eaten, like any regular מנחה. A בת ישראל married to a כהן also has the handful taken, but as the משנה says, the rest of her מנחה is burned and not eaten.

keyTerms.meaning: A כהן's meal-offering
Completely burned on the altar
A daughter of a כהן
As the פסוק says

steps.confusionAlert: Two different 'burnings' are involved here. A כהן's own מנחה is כליל: all of it goes on the altar. A בת ישראל married to a כהן is not a 'כהן', so her מנחה is not כליל and the handful is still taken. But the rest of her מנחה is not eaten; it is burned, as the משנה says.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר קְרָא: ״וְכׇל מִנְחַת כֹּהֵן כָּלִיל תִּהְיֶה
phrases.english: As the verse states: "And every meal-offering of a priest shall be completely burned;
it shall not be eaten."
A priest, and not a priest's daughter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק says 'כהן', which means a male כהן and not a כהנת.

steps.title: Why can a priest's daughter be disqualified but not a priest?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: a כהנת can become disqualified, but a כהן cannot. It asks for the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: a כהנת becomes disqualified, but a כהן does not become disqualified. Where do we learn this from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next difference in the משנה and asks for its source. This step sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כהנת who has relations with someone forbidden to her becomes a חללה. She can then no longer marry a כהן or eat תרומה. A כהן who has relations with a woman forbidden to him does not lose his own status. The גמרא wants a פסוק that shows this.

keyTerms.meaning: She becomes a חללה; she loses her כהונה status
From where do we know this?

phrases.english: A priest's daughter becomes disqualified; a priest does not become disqualified.
From where do we derive this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next line of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the source that a כהן does not become a חלל through forbidden relations?

steps.title: His children are disqualified, but he is not
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'ולא יחלל זרעו' says that his children become חללים. It says nothing about him, so he himself stays a כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'He shall not make his children חללים among his people.' His children become חללים, but he himself does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק that speaks about a כהן's children becoming disqualified. This shows that the כהן himself is not disqualified.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק could have said that the כהן himself is made a חלל, but it only mentions 'זרעו', his children. From this we learn that a forbidden marriage hurts the status of his children, not his own status.

keyTerms.meaning: Make into a חלל; disqualify
His children

phrases.english: As the verse states: "And he shall not disqualify his offspring among his people."
His offspring become disqualified, but he does not become disqualified.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק names only 'זרעו', his children, as becoming חללים. The כהן himself does not.

steps.title: Why may a priest's daughter become impure from the dead?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: a כהנת may become impure from a dead body, but a כהן may not. It asks for the reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: a כהנת may become impure... What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא takes up the third difference in the משנה and asks for its source. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כהן is forbidden to become impure from a dead body (טומאת מת). A כהנת is allowed to. The גמרא asks what source teaches that the איסור does not apply to women.

keyTerms.meaning: She may become impure (from a dead body)
Etc.; short for וכו׳

phrases.english: A priest's daughter may become impure, etc.
phrases.notes: The rest of the משנה: but a כהן may not become impure from a dead body.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the third difference in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the source that a כהנת may become impure from a dead body?

steps.title: Sons of אהרן, not daughters of אהרן
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'אמר אל הכהנים בני אהרן' is said to the sons of אהרן. So the איסור of טומאת מת does not apply to his daughters.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'Speak to the כהנים, the sons of אהרן.' The sons of אהרן, and not the daughters of אהרן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with the פסוק that opens the איסור of טומאת מת for כהנים. It is addressed only to 'בני אהרן', the sons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק could have just said 'the כהנים', but it adds 'בני אהרן'. This limits the איסור to males. Just like the two answers before it, the rule depends on wording in the פסוק that refers to a male כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: Speak to the כהנים (the start of the פרשה about כהנים)
The sons of אהרן
The daughters of אהרן

steps.whatToRemember: All three differences between a כהן and a כהנת come from wording in the פסוק that refers to the male: 'כהן', 'זרעו' (and not him), and 'בני אהרן'.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר קְרָא: ״אֱמֹר אֶל הַכֹּהֲנִים בְּנֵי אַהֲרֹן״.
phrases.english: The verse states: "Speak to the priests, the sons of Aaron."
The sons of Aaron, and not the daughters of Aaron.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק is addressed to 'בני אהרן', so the איסור of טומאת מת applies to the sons and not to the daughters.

steps.title: Only a male כהן eats the most holy offerings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה that a כהן eats קדשי קדשים and brings the פסוק that says only males may eat them.
steps.simpleTranslation: A כהן eats from the most holy offerings, because the פסוק says: 'Every male among the sons of אהרן shall eat it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה and right away gives its source from a פסוק. The question 'from where do we know?' is understood without being said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'every male,' so eating קדשי קדשים is only for male כהנים. A בת כהן can eat other holy food like תרומה, but not קדשי קדשים. This follows the same pattern as the earlier steps: quote the משנה, then show the word in the פסוק that leaves out women.

keyTerms.meaning: The most holy offerings, which have stricter rules about who may eat them
Male
As it is written (a פסוק is being brought)

phrases.english: A priest eats from the most holy offerings,
as it is written: "Every male among the sons of Aaron shall eat it."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next item in the same list of differences between a כהן and a כהנת, with the question left unsaid and the source given right away.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'כל זכר בבני אהרן יאכלנה' limits eating קדשי קדשים to males.

steps.title: The word איש seems to leave out women from the laws of a מצורע
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves to the next part of the משנה, about a man and a woman. A ברייתא notes that the פסוק says 'איש' and asks how we know the laws of a מצורע apply to a woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And what is the difference between a man...' The רבנן taught: The פסוק says 'a man.' That only teaches about a man. From where do we know it applies to a woman?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new section of the משנה and brings a ברייתא. The ברייתא starts by asking a question it is about to answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about a confirmed מצורע says 'איש צרוע הוא,' a leprous man. Read alone, that word could mean the whole set of מצורע laws is only for men. The ברייתא is looking for a source that includes women.

keyTerms.meaning: The רבנן taught (introduces a ברייתא)
I only know (this case), and nothing more yet
From where do we know?
A person with צרעת, a spiritual skin disease

phrases.english: "And what is the difference between a man," etc.
phrases.notes: The rest of the משנה: a man lets his hair grow and tears his clothes as a מצורע, but a woman does not.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
"Man": I only know about a man.
From where do we know a woman?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין לִי אֶלָּא אִישׁ. אִשָּׁה מִנַּיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the כהן/כהנת list to the next section of the משנה about איש and אשה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that the laws of a מצורע apply to a woman, even though the פסוק says 'איש'.

steps.title: An extra word in the next פסוק includes a woman
steps.stepSummary: The next פסוק repeats 'והצרוע,' which was not needed, so it adds a second person: a woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the פסוק says 'And the leper in whom the plague is,' that means there are two here.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own question. It points to a word in the next פסוק that seems extra.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already knew from the earlier פסוק who the מצורע was, so the פסוק did not need to say 'והצרוע' again. Since the word is extra, it comes to add someone else: a woman. So the laws of צרעת apply to both a man and a woman.

keyTerms.meaning: When the פסוק says (introduces a proof from a פסוק)
Here there are two, meaning two kinds of people are included

phrases.english: When it says "And the leper in whom the plague is":
here there are two,
phrases.notes: The פסוק didn't need to say 'the leper' again, so it's adding a second person: a woman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra word 'והצרוע' includes a woman in the laws of a מצורע.

steps.title: So why does the פסוק say איש at all?
steps.stepSummary: If women are included in צרעת, the ברייתא asks what the word 'איש' comes to teach.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why does the פסוק say 'a man'?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that women are included, the ברייתא asks what the word 'איש' is there for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah does not use words for nothing. Since 'איש' can no longer leave women out of צרעת as a whole, it must be teaching something else. This sets up the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
Why does the פסוק say it? (what does this word come to teach?)

phrases.english: If so, what does the verse teach by saying "man"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from step 10: if women are included, the word 'איש' now needs a new purpose.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the word 'איש' teaches, now that it does not leave women out of צרעת.

steps.title: איש teaches that only a man tears his clothes and grows his hair
steps.stepSummary: The word 'איש' points to the law in the next פסוק: only a male מצורע lets his hair grow and tears his clothes.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is for the matter written below: a man lets his hair grow, and so on, but a woman does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes by giving 'איש' its job. It limits the hair and clothing laws to men.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A woman is a מצורע in every other way, including being טמא. Only the public mourning signs, growing the hair wild and tearing the clothes, are for a man alone. This is exactly the difference the משנה listed.

keyTerms.meaning: For the matter written below (in the next פסוק)
Lets the hair of his head grow wild

steps.whatToRemember: A woman is a full מצורע. The word 'איש' only takes her out of the laws of growing the hair and tearing the clothes.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think a woman cannot become a מצורע. She can. 'איש' only leaves her out of the hair and clothing laws.

phrases.english: for the matter written below,
a man lets his hair grow, etc.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 11 and closes the מצורע section.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: 'איש' teaches that only a male מצורע grows his hair and tears his clothes. All other laws of צרעת apply to women too.

steps.title: Only a father can make his son a נזיר: a הלכה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says a man can vow to make his young son a נזיר, but a woman cannot. רבי יוחנן says this is a הלכה with no פסוק behind it.
steps.simpleTranslation: A man can make his son a נזיר, but a woman cannot make her son a נזיר. רבי יוחנן said: This is a הלכה about a נזיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next difference in the משנה. רבי יוחנן explains its source: it is a הלכה, not something learned from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now each difference came from a word in a פסוק. Here there is no פסוק. The rule is a הלכה למשה מסיני, a law passed down orally from משה.

keyTerms.meaning: Makes someone else bound by a vow
A person who vowed not to drink wine, not to cut his hair, and not to become טמא from the dead
Here: a הלכה למשה מסיני, a law handed down orally from משה, not from a פסוק

phrases.english: A man may vow that his son be a nazirite,
phrases.notes: This means a young son who hasn't grown up yet.

phrases.english: but a woman may not vow that her son be a nazirite.
Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
It is a halakha regarding a nazirite.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, הֲלָכָה הִיא בְּנָזִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next item in the משנה's list. Its source is a הלכה instead of a פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only a father, not a mother, can make a young son a נזיר. This is a הלכה למשה מסיני.

steps.title: A son may use his father's נזירות offerings: also a הלכה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says a son may use what his father set aside for his own נזירות offerings to finish the son's נזירות, but a daughter may not. רבי יוחנן says this too is a הלכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A man may shave using his father's נזירות, but a woman may not shave using her father's נזירות. רבי יוחנן said: This is a הלכה about a נזיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the last difference in this list. רבי יוחנן again says it comes from a הלכה, not from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נזיר ends his נזירות by shaving and bringing offerings. If a father who was a נזיר set aside money for his own נזירות offerings and died before using it, his son who is a נזיר may use it for his own shaving offerings. A daughter may not, and the source is a הלכה למשה מסיני.

keyTerms.meaning: Shaves, meaning finishes his נזירות with the shaving and its offerings
The state of being a נזיר, and here the offerings set aside for it

steps.whatToRemember: Two differences between men and women in נזירות, making a son a נזיר and using a father's offerings, come from a הלכה למשה מסיני, not from a פסוק.

phrases.english: A man may shave using his father's naziriteship,
phrases.notes: He finishes his own נזירות using the offerings his father set aside for his father's נזירות.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין הָאִשָּׁה מְגַלַּחַת עַל נְזִירוּת אָבִיהָ.
phrases.english: but a woman may not shave using her father's naziriteship.
Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
It is a halakha regarding a nazirite.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: הֲלָכָה הִיא בְּנָזִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows the same pattern as step 13 with a second נזיר law.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A son, but not a daughter, may use his father's נזירות offerings for his own shaving. This is a הלכה למשה מסיני.

steps.title: Only a father can arrange his daughter's betrothal
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says a father can arrange קידושין for his daughter, but a mother cannot. The source is a פסוק where the father says 'I gave my daughter.'
steps.simpleTranslation: A man can betroth his daughter, but a woman cannot betroth her daughter, as it says: 'I gave my daughter to this man.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה and gives its source from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פסוק, the father is the one speaking about giving his daughter in marriage. That shows the power to arrange her קידושין belongs to him and not to her mother.

keyTerms.meaning: Betroths; here, arranges the קידושין of his young daughter
As it is written
His daughter

phrases.english: A man can betroth his daughter,
but a woman cannot betroth her daughter.
As it is written:
"I gave my daughter to this man."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next item in the משנה's list of male-female differences. This time the source is a פסוק, not a הלכה with no פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only a father can arrange קידושין for his daughter.

steps.title: Only a father can sell his daughter as a maidservant
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says a father can sell his young daughter as an אמה העבריה, but a mother cannot. The פסוק says 'a man sells his daughter.'
steps.simpleTranslation: A man can sell his daughter, but a woman cannot sell her daughter, as it says: 'And if a man sells his daughter.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source for the next line of the משנה: the פסוק speaks only about a man selling his daughter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'איש' (a man) is the one who sells. So this power is given only to the father.

keyTerms.meaning: Sells
Will sell (the word in the פסוק)
A man; the word that limits the law to the father

phrases.english: A man can sell his daughter,
but a woman cannot sell her daughter.
As it is written:
"And if a man sells his daughter."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same pattern as step 15, applied to selling a daughter.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only a father can sell his daughter as an אמה העבריה.

steps.title: Why a man is stoned without clothes
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says a man is stoned naked. The גמרא asks for the source and points to the פסוק 'and they shall stone him.'
steps.simpleTranslation: 'A man is stoned naked, etc.' What is the reason? Because it says: 'And they shall stone him.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה about סקילה, asks for the reason, and answers with the word 'אותו' (him) in a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof rests on the extra word 'אותו.' What exactly this word teaches is not yet clear, so the גמרא will look into it in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: Is stoned (put to death by סקילה)
Naked, without clothes
What is the reason?
And they shall stone

phrases.english: A man is stoned naked, etc.
phrases.notes: 'כו׳' means 'and so on.' The משנה continues: but a woman is not stoned naked.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
"And they shall stone him."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new line of the משנה, about סקילה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that a man is stoned naked and a woman is not.

steps.title: What does the word 'him' teach?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what exactly the word 'אותו' comes to teach.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'him' come to teach?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup question. The גמרא wants to pin down what 'אותו' leaves out, and it will test two possible answers next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'אותו' seems to leave something out, but it is not clear what. It could leave out women completely, or it could leave out something else.

keyTerms.meaning: What
Him
What is the word 'him' for?

phrases.english: What does "him" come to teach?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the exact meaning of the source word given in step 17.

steps.title: 'Him' cannot mean women are never stoned
steps.stepSummary: One idea is that 'אותו' means only a man is stoned. But another פסוק says 'that man or that woman' is taken out to be stoned.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it means 'him and not her,' but it is written: 'And you shall take out that man or that woman'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the simplest reading, that women are not stoned at all, and knocks it down with another פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in דברים clearly includes a woman in the punishment of סקילה. So 'אותו' cannot remove women from being stoned.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introduces an idea that will be rejected)
But isn't it written?
And you shall take out

steps.confusionAlert: Women are stoned for capital sins just like men. The question here is only how the stoning is done, not whether it happens.

phrases.english: If you say: him and not her,
but isn't it written:
"And you shall take out that man
or that woman"!
phrases.notes: דברים 17:5. That פסוק goes on to say they are stoned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests one possible answer to step 18 and rejects it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that 'אותו' means a woman is not stoned at all.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another פסוק clearly says a woman is stoned.

steps.title: 'Him' means without his clothes
steps.stepSummary: The real meaning is that 'אותו' means him, without his clothing. A woman is not stoned without her clothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: him without his clothing, but not her without her clothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the correct meaning of 'אותו,' and this explains the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'אותו' is read as 'him himself,' meaning his body alone, without his clothes. Since the word is male, this applies only to a man. A woman is stoned, but she stays clothed.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (introduces the correct answer)
His clothing
Her

steps.whatToRemember: Both men and women receive סקילה. The word 'אותו' teaches only that a man is stoned without clothes and a woman is not.

phrases.english: Rather:
"him" means him without his clothing,
but not her without her clothing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a new reading of 'אותו' after step 19 ruled out the first one.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the word: it leaves out clothing, not women.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'אותו' leaves out women from סקילה altogether.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'אותו' means a man is stoned without clothes. A woman is stoned clothed.

steps.title: Only a man is hanged
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says a man is hanged after his execution but a woman is not. The פסוק says 'you shall hang him.'
steps.simpleTranslation: 'A man is hanged, but a woman is not, etc.' What is the reason? The verse says: 'And you shall hang him on a tree.' Him, and not her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the משנה's rule about תלייה and answers from the word 'אותו.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here 'אותו' really does leave out women. No other פסוק says a woman is hanged, so the simple reading works here, unlike with stoning.

keyTerms.meaning: Is hanged
The verse says
A tree, a wooden post

phrases.english: A man is hanged, but a woman is not, etc.
What is the reason?
The verse says:
"And you shall hang him on a tree,"
him, and not her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next line of the משנה. The same word 'אותו' works here in its simple sense.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that only a man is hanged.

steps.title: Only a man is sold for his theft
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says a man who cannot pay back what he stole is sold, but a woman is not. The פסוק says 'he shall be sold for his theft.'
steps.simpleTranslation: A man is sold for his theft, but a woman is not sold for her theft. What is the reason? The verse says: 'He shall be sold for his theft.' For his theft, not for her theft.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source for the last line of the משנה here: the פסוק speaks of 'his' theft.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The male form 'בגניבתו' (his theft) limits being sold as a servant to a man. A woman who steals and cannot pay is not sold.

keyTerms.meaning: Is sold (as a servant)
His theft

steps.whatToRemember: For each difference in this משנה, the גמרא points to a male word in a פסוק, like 'איש' or 'אותו.' The exceptions are the rules רבי יוחנן called a הלכה with no פסוק.

phrases.english: A man is sold for his theft,
but a woman is not sold for her theft.
What is the reason? The verse says:
"Then he shall be sold for his theft,"
for his theft, and not for her theft.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same pattern as step 21, applied to being sold for theft.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that only a man is sold for theft.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק היה נוטל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא formally finishes the third פרק of מסכת סוטה, called היה נוטל.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק 'היה נוטל'.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the closing line for the פרק we just finished. Nothing new is argued here. It is a marker that one chapter is over and a new one is about to start.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A הדרן line is said at the end of every פרק and expresses a hope to come back and learn it again. The chapter is named for its opening words, 'היה נוטל'.

keyTerms.meaning: 'We will return to you': the formula said when finishing a פרק
A chapter of the משנה and גמרא

steps.whatToRemember: פרק היה נוטל is finished here. Everything after this belongs to a new chapter.

phrases.english: We will return to you, 'He would take'
phrases.notes: 'He would take' is the name of the chapter, taken from its opening words.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the entire chapter whose last discussion ended in step 22.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The third פרק of סוטה, היה נוטל, is complete.

steps.title: A betrothed woman and a widow waiting for her brother-in-law do not drink
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה rules that an ארוסה and a שומרת יבם neither drink the סוטה water nor collect a כתובה. It brings a פסוק to show they are excluded from drinking.
steps.simpleTranslation: An ארוסה and a שומרת יבם do not drink and do not collect a כתובה, because the פסוק says 'when a wife goes astray while under her husband.' This leaves out an ארוסה and a שומרת יבם.
steps.whatsHappening: The new פרק opens with a משנה listing two women who are left out of the סוטה drinking. It brings a פסוק as the source for leaving them out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks of a woman who is 'under her husband,' meaning she is actually married and living with him. An ארוסה is only betrothed, and a שומרת יבם is still waiting for the יבם to marry her, so neither one counts as 'under her husband.' The משנה adds that they also lose their כתובה, but it does not give the reason for that part here.

keyTerms.meaning: A betrothed woman: she has had קידושין but is not yet fully married
A widow waiting for her late husband's brother to do יבום
The marriage contract money a woman receives when the marriage ends
'Under her husband': actually married to him
'Excluding': the פסוק leaves out this case

steps.confusionAlert: The פסוק is brought only to explain why they do not drink. Do not assume it also explains why they lose the כתובה, because the משנה does not say that here.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the theme of the whole new פרק: which women are outside the סוטה process, and what happens to their כתובה.

phrases.english: A betrothed woman and a widow waiting for her brother-in-law
do not drink and do not collect a marriage contract,
phrases.notes: 'Drink' means drinking the bitter water of a סוטה.

phrases.english: as it says: 'when a wife goes astray while under her husband,'
excluding a betrothed woman and a widow waiting for her brother-in-law.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲרוּסָה וְשׁוֹמֶרֶת יָבָם לֹא שׁוֹתוֹת וְלֹא נוֹטְלוֹת כְּתוּבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the new פרק (ארוסה) right after the הדרן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An ארוסה and a שומרת יבם do not drink and do not get a כתובה. The exclusion from drinking comes from 'תחת אישה'.

steps.title: Beginning the list of women in forbidden marriages
steps.stepSummary: The משנה starts a new list: a widow married to a כהן גדול, a divorcee or חלוצה married to a כהן הדיוט, and a ממזרת. The list and its ruling continue in the next section.
steps.simpleTranslation: A widow married to a כהן גדול, a divorcee or חלוצה married to a regular כהן, a ממזרת…
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה is setting up its next case by listing women whose marriages were forbidden from the start. The ruling about them has not come yet and continues in the next section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה has moved from women who are not yet fully married to women who are married, but whose marriages break a Torah prohibition. Each pair here is a forbidden match: a כהן גדול may not marry a widow, and any כהן may not marry a גרושה or a חלוצה. The ממזרת begins a further case whose details come next.

keyTerms.meaning: A widow
The High Priest, who may not marry a widow
A divorced woman, forbidden to any כהן
A woman released from יבום through חליצה, forbidden to a כהן
A regular כהן, not the כהן גדול
A female ממזר, born from a forbidden union

phrases.english: A widow married to a High Priest,
a divorcee or a חלוצה married to a regular priest,
a mamzeret

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלְמָנָה לְכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל גְּרוּשָׁה וַחֲלוּצָה לְכֹהֵן הֶדְיוֹט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה with a new category of women: those in forbidden marriages instead of incomplete ones.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Lists women in forbidden marriages. The ruling for them comes in the continuation of the משנה.
